Dishes featuring on the menu here include matured raw fish with ajoblanco, octopus with a roasted and creamy tomato rice and basil farofa, and boneless fish of the day served with creamy lemon rice. In addition to the relaxed atmosphere, the wonderful sunsets are one of OCYÁ Ilha’s major attractions!

rows.name: Kubo Zushi
rows.address: Rua Das Tabocas 158, São Paulo, 05445-020, Brazil
rows.description_en: If you’re looking for a classic Japanese dining experience that is truly authentic and steers clear of any form of contemporary influence, especially when it comes to sushi and sashimi, this is the perfect restaurant for you. Here, to a backdrop of simple decor in the residential Vila Madalena district, chef Sergio Kubo prepare edomae sushi, a culinary tradition mastered over many years. The high quality of ingredients is clearly evident in dishes such tuna tartare, tartare with salmon roe, and tobiko and quail egg yolk, as well as an array of combinations. The restaurant is divided into three sections, although it is obvious that the sushi bar is the heart and soul of the property, where guests will enjoy watching and admiring the skill of Kubo Zushi’s chefs. There’s even an attractive play area for kids!

rows.name: Vinheria Percussi
rows.address: Rua Bianchi Bertoldi 109, São Paulo, 05422-070, Brazil
rows.description_en: A family-run Italian restaurant that was a trailblazer for enogastronomy (the pairing of food and wine) in Brazil. It first opened as a wine shop in 1985 with the aim of offering good wine and food to go with it. However, with the arrival of chef Silvia Percussi and her brother Lamberto Percussi (restaurant manager and sommelier) the concept was taken to the next level. In this classic, welcoming setting, enjoy excellent cuisine including fresh pasta, which is a particular highlight. Classic dishes that you’ll want to try include the perfectly creamy tonnarelli alla carbonara, the beef ossobuco, served with a divine sauce, and the tiramisu, which is brought to your table on a platter. Why not pair these delicacies with one of the fines wines on the 300-strong wine list and in the award-winning cellar.

rows.name: Cais
rows.address: Rua Fidalga 314, São Paulo, 05432-000, Brazil
rows.description_en: A relaxed restaurant with a lively atmosphere and good food, so it’s not surprising that it’s always full. Occupying a charming small house in the Vila Madalena neighbourhood of the city, Cais features tables outdoors next to the window, seats at the counter by the kitchen, as well more traditional tables. Run by Adriano de Laurentiis in the kitchen and chef Catarina Ferraz, its cuisine is centred around fresh fish and seafood. The concise menu is constantly updated in line with the availability and freshness of seasonal ingredients. Having savoured the delicious appetisers on offer here, we particularly recommend the week’s selection of fish and seafood, followed by the creamy and delicate cheesecake served with a milk sorbet.

rows.name: Giulietta Carni
rows.address: Rua Jerônimo Da Veiga 36, São Paulo, 04536-000, Brazil
rows.description_en: Located in one of the city’s business districts, this attractive restaurant comes as a pleasant surprise thanks to its unusual Italian-churrascaria fusion. It combines an industrial design and glass-fronted, open-view kitchen with an array of kitschy decorative details—note the paintings of animals with their aristocratic poses and clothing. The cooking here is traditionally Italian but with a good dash of creativity, and a focus on dishes cooked on the grill or in the oven, such as the mouthwatering glazed beef rib with a Gran Masala sauce, potato millefeuille and roasted onions. Reservations are highly recommended if you’re planning on having dinner here.

rows.name: Mondo
rows.address: Rua Oscar Freire 30, São Paulo, 01426-000, Brazil
rows.description_en: If you’re looking for a restaurant where you can enjoy excellent Italian cuisine, this is definitely the right place! Located at the end of the famous Rua Oscar Freire, it boasts an elegant glass façade and a spacious interior, with an open kitchen to the rear. The cooking revolves around classic Italian recipes, including pasta, but without neglecting generous dishes of fish and meat. The menu is teeming with amazing options, including “ravioli al tuorlo”, stuffed with ricotta, spinach and melted parmesan and served with a creamy egg yolk, and “pappardele con ragù d'ossobuco”. If you still have an appetite, we also recommend the majestic “filetto alla rossini”, served with black truffle and potato millefeuille. A midday “mezzogiorno” menu option is also available midweek.

rows.name: El Tranvia - Itaim Bibi
rows.address: Rua Leopoldo Couto de Magalhães 1372, São Paulo, 03178-200, Brazil
rows.description_en: Those who head to this restaurant should be in no doubt as to its reputation as a culinary institution showcasing the very best flavours of traditional Uruguayan cooking. The beef served here is of exceptional quality and includes numerous choice cuts (beef short ribs, strip loin, sirloin etc) and matured meat options that are enhanced to the full over the flames of the parrilla. You’ll also find fillets of meat of all types and sizes to cater to the many families from every generation who flock here, with the quantity of side dishes depending on the number of guests at the table. The fries and the delicious Uruguayan flan with “dulce de leche” are a must.

rows.name: Lassù
rows.address: Rua Conselheiro Saraiva 207, São Paulo, 02037-020, Brazil
rows.description_en: If the idea of an incredible dining experience coupled with breathtaking views appeals to you, Lassù is able to combine both at the same time. With a location on the 28th floor of the lofty Edifício K1 in the Zona Norte district, this restaurant boasts one of the most impressive views of the city, with some tables enjoying a 270° perspective. The ambience here is both refined and elegant, enhanced by subtle lighting and a charming bar on one side of the dining room. The cuisine is a mix of Italian influences and ingredients from Brazil’s different regions. Standout dishes include the unmissable cod brandade served with black olive farofa, and the exquisite “lasagna ristorantino” with black truffle. The space also has the Lassù Rooftop Club, which makes it possible to celebrate exclusive events, besides a feijoada buffet, accompanied by Brazilian desserts and live music on Saturday afternoons!

rows.name: Sal Gastronomia
rows.address: Rua Bela Cintra 1958, São Paulo, 01415-006, Brazil
rows.description_en: There are very few Brazilians who are not familiar with chef Henrique Fogaça, who is extremely popular thanks to his role as a judge on MasterChef as well being the lead singer for the hardcore band Oitão. Behind Sal Gastronomia’s unique pirate-inspired logo (a skull with a knife and fork) is a contemporary-style restaurant featuring industrial decorative decor, which provides the backdrop for modern Brazilian cuisine on an à la carte and two tasting menus. The sort of dishes you’ll find here include scallops with a chestnut cream and pupunha heart of palm; fish of the day with a plantain moqueca stew; and beef ribs with cassava purée, watercress pesto and cheese curd.

rows.name: Bar da Dona Onça
rows.address: Avenida Ipiranga 200, São Paulo, 01046-925, Brazil
rows.description_en: Ideally situated in the historic heart of São Paulo — more precisely, on the ground floor of the Edifício Copan, an iconic wave-shaped skyscraper designed by the celebrated Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer — this is a buzzing, unpretentious, and enormously popular restaurant; so much so that queuing at the door for a table is entirely the norm. The culinary concept, under the direction of chef Janaína Torres (recognised as one of the most important and influential chefs in the world), celebrates the flavours of Brazil's interior through a wonderfully broad menu spanning all manner of dishes — sharing starters, stews, pasta, fish, and meat — all rooted in traditional taste and artisanal preparation. One dish that never disappoints is the succulent picadinho, a classic Brazilian beef hash served with rice, a fried egg, a crispy pastel filled with meat, and banana tartare. The bar, which is almost always packed, turns out delicious and refreshing cocktails!

rows.name: Sushi Leblon
rows.address: Rua Dias Ferreira 256, Rio de Janeiro, 22431-050, Brazil
rows.description_en: An exclusive space with a trendy (and renowned) atmosphere in the southern part of Rio de Janeiro, where it has become a popular choice for those who enjoy high-quality Japanese cuisine. Open for almost four decades, the place is always on the up as it maintains its sense of tradition without turning its back on emerging food trends. In an intimate space decorated with a mix of dark tones and wood, the most sought-after spot is the bar counter by the kitchen where incredible dishes such as cubes of salmon with chilli pepper and truffle oil are served. Other options include the unmissable tuna tartare with free-range egg yolk and black roe, “combinados”, sushi, sashimi etc. At lunchtime, there’s more flexibility if you don’t have a reservation, but we recommend booking ahead for dinner.

rows.name: Escama
rows.address: Rua Visconde de Carandaí, 5, Rio de Janeiro, 22460 020, Brazil
rows.description_en: After visiting a French restaurant with a similar outlook, inspiration struck to open this restaurant serving the best fish and seafood in a relaxed ambience. The focus at Escama is one that showcases the best maritime ingredients, which he always sources fresh from local fishermen. For your main, you can choose how you want to have your fish prepared (grilled, baked or poached), such as the sea bass, which is accompanied by a delicious champagne sauce and roasted onions. The menu also features options such as squid, shrimp, scallops and oysters, plus a splendid seafood feijoada on Fridays. The restaurant is located close to the city’s botanical garden, in a charming two-floor property with an extremely relaxed ambience enhanced by a decor of muted colours.

rows.name: Bistrot de Paris
rows.address: Rua Augusta 2542, São Paulo, 01412-100, Brazil
rows.description_en: This romantic, welcoming spot, hidden at the end of the corridor of the charming Villa San Pietro on Rua Augusta, gives you the delicious feeling of stepping into an authentic Parisian bistro. Led by renowned French chef Alain Poletto, the restaurant serves classic French cuisine based on traditional recipes and top-quality ingredients. Among the tempting starters are Charcuterias dos Alpes Caseiras, house-made Alpine charcuterie, Foie Gras and Patê de Campagne, all prepared in-house. The main course, Beef Wellington carved at the table, served with a fine golden crust, perfectly cooked meat and an irresistible Port-wine reduction with truffles, and the dessert, Riz au Lait with sea-salt caramel and caramelised cashews, deliver that Paris-in-São-Paulo moment. The drinks available to accompany the meal only enrich the experience further!

rows.name: La Villa - Bistrô Francês
rows.address: Rua Alvaro Ramos 408, Rio de Janeiro, 22280-110, Brazil
rows.description_en: This French brasserie occupies a unique property in Botafogo dating back to 1775 and has established itself as a trusted option for those who enjoy authentic Gallic cuisine. Under the management of French owner Gregoire Fortat, La Villa features a simple decor, high ceilings, outdoor tables and a pleasant and hospitable ambience. The menu here is centred around traditional French bistro fare with an added Brazilian touch. The experience begins with a delicious pâté de champagne served with bread baked on the premises, followed by the classic onion soup, and an authentic duck cassoulet. On Sundays, there’s also a French-Brazilian barbecue including an impressive array of fish and seafood.

rows.name: Goya Zushi
rows.address: Rua Artur Frazão, 37, São Paulo, 01423-030, Brazil
rows.description_en: Looking for a Japanese restaurant in the Jardim Paulista area? This one won't disappoint — it is the kind of place where everything revolves around a U-shaped counter seating eleven, and where a single, ever-evolving omakase menu takes centre stage, shaped entirely by whatever is in season. Chef Uilian Goya, ably supported by Lucas Ryu, does everything in his power to ensure guests feel at ease and can fully appreciate the craft behind each step — a craft rooted in kaiseki culinary philosophy, the Japanese tradition of a multi-course meal that follows the rhythm of the seasons. The highlight comes during the sushi course, where you will witness the meticulous preparation of the traditional rice: mixed in a wooden bowl, damp cloth at the ready, a paddle, a generous splash of red vinegar… and the final, airy result taking shape right before your eyes. Your menu will be waiting at your place, handwritten with the day's dishes and the name on your reservation. One word of advice, though — punctuality matters, so that everyone can begin together!

rows.name: Nelita
rows.address: Rua Ferreira De Araújo, 330, São Paulo, 05428-000, Brazil
rows.description_en: One of the standout restaurants in the Baixo Pinheiros area! This establishment, under the direction of chef Tássia Magalhães — who leads an all-female kitchen team — offers an enticing menu of Italian-influenced signature dishes. On the floor, the wine list is carefully curated by Danyel Steinle, who champions Brazilian labels without overlooking international references, ensuring pairings that are both precise and elegant. The experience is divided into three formats: the 11-course Experiência menu, served exclusively at the kitchen counter, a 6-course menu inspired by the delicacy and strength of female cooking, and an à la carte menu. In addition to the option of sitting at the chef's counter, the space — decorated in a modern style with a variety of distinct areas — offers tables throughout the dining room and a private room that can be reserved for groups.

rows.name: Nôa Ipanema
rows.address: Rua Garcia D'Ávila, 135, Rio de Janeiro, 22421-010, Brazil
rows.description_en: This lively restaurant sits in one of Ipanema’s most buzzed-about areas, in a charming 1930s house, and pairs the neighbourhood’s vibrant essence with a warm, welcoming culinary concept. In a space defined by minimalist décor, where Hebrew-inspired paintings adorn the walls, you’ll find international cooking rooted in Brazilian cuisine with French touches. Alongside salads, meats, fish, seafood and fresh pasta, you can choose the fresh fish of the day and pair it with a side dish. Our suggestion? Arroz de moqueca com camarões grelhados, moqueca rice with grilled prawns, and for dessert, Tarta Basca, Basque cheesecake, served with goiabada syrup and cheese ice cream. Enjoy the charming veranda with the refreshing cocktails on offer!

rows.name: Ama.zo - Pátio Higienópolis
rows.address: Avenida Higienópolis 618, São Paulo, 01238-001, Brazil
rows.description_en: Located outside of the Pátio Higienópolis shopping mall, it features an attractive room with lots of natural light and an open-air terrace decorated with plants and Peruvian works of art. Here, the Lima-born chef Enrique Paredes, whose philosophy is “Cooking with freedom”, is at the helm of his second venture, where he combines Peruvian flavours and techniques with local ingredients to showcase the flavours of the Amazon, without losing sight of the region’s roots. On the menu you’ll find dishes such as langoustine carpaccio, the traditional Lima dish “causa limeña”, along with various types of ceviche, rice dishes and vegetarian and vegan options. One dessert that you won’t want to pass up is the “Suspiro Limeño” made with delicious Peruvian “dulce de leche”, a dehydrated quinoa and togarashi meringue, praline and chocolate sorbet – a true delight for the tastebuds!

rows.name: OCYÁ Leblon
rows.address: Rua Aristides Espínola, 88, Rio de Janeiro, 22440-050, Brazil
rows.description_en: Fisherman, diver, and chef Gerônimo Athuel is a true fountain of knowledge when it comes to seafood. His priority is to champion the importance of sustainable, selective, and artisanal fishing, and he is deeply committed to researching techniques for preservation, ageing, and the whole-fish approach to species that are typically discarded, bringing them into his kitchen. With one location on Ilha Primeira, the chef has expanded his concept to the Zona Sul, in an entirely distinctive space flooded with natural light, with modern décor and a glass ageing chamber displayed right at the entrance, underscoring the restaurant's ethos. The offering features some surprising options, from ocean charcuterie to grilled, fried, and raw fish… One of the standout dishes on the menu that we absolutely loved was the aged fish served with a grape and almond sauce!

rows.name: Babbo Osteria
rows.address: Rua Barão Da Torre, 632, Rio de Janeiro, 22411 002, Brazil
rows.description_en: An outstanding property in a quiet residential section of Ipanema, whose Italian name (“babbo” is a colloquial Italian word for “dad”) provides an insight into the cuisine served here, a fusion of Italian and “carioca” dishes conjured up by chef Elia Schramm. One of the most popular eateries in the area, Babbo Osteria pays homage to the chef's father, and brings childhood memories and family influences to the cooking on offer. One of the dining rooms, decorated with ornaments reminiscent of a traditional Italian “osteria”, provides the backdrop for handmade pasta dishes such as Uova Pepenara (tagliolini served with small cubes of bacon and a creamy soft egg) – the chef's version of the classic carbonara. Main courses include the “filetto”, a medallion served with a delicious pepper sauce and golden gnocchi, as well as desserts in the purest Italian style, such as tiramisù and a perfect combination of pistachio and lime!

rows.name: De Segunda
rows.address: Rua Prof. Tamandaré Toledo, 160, São Paulo, 04532-020, Brazil
rows.description_en: Young chefs Júlia Tricate and Gabriel Coelho already have impressive CVs, having won TV food competitions and worked in Michelin-starred restaurants such as Noma (Copenhagen) and Oro (Rio de Janeiro). Following on from these incredible experiences, they decided to open their own restaurant with an open kitchen and a discreet decor that helps to channel the complete focus onto their cuisine. Their modern culinary vision is showcased on a creative menu that champions fresh, seasonal ingredients on a tasting menu, à la carte and midweek “executive” menu”. Combinations such as the pork rib cooked for 12 hours and served with a meat glaze hummus and fried onion, and the restaurant’s classic take on hump of beef, here accompanied by a creamy sweet potato and gorgonzola purée, will definitely leave a lasting memory of this restaurant.

rows.name: Haru Sushi Bar
rows.address: Rua Raimuindo Corrêa, 10, Rio de Janeiro, 22040-042, Brazil
rows.description_en: Chef Menandro (Nandro) Rodrigues's passion for Japanese cooking is the driving force behind this welcoming restaurant, right in the heart of the Copacabana neighbourhood. On the ground floor, there are tables on the pavement and a relaxed, informal service; upstairs, a Japanese-styled dining room houses an impressive counter facing the open kitchen, with tables spread across several distinct areas. Faithful to the Japanese philosophy of Kaizen — which means continuous improvement — the chef dedicates particular care to both his techniques and his produce, sourced directly from local fishermen. Here, you can choose between the omakase menu or a variety of sushi, sashimi, temaki, and traditional or special combination platters — but for those seeking a truly singular experience, it is well worth booking a seat at UMAI, a more private and elegant counter nestled within Haru Sushi Bar like a restaurant within a restaurant, where a single omakase menu is served across 16 courses. A wide selection of sake is also on offer, available by the glass too!

rows.name: Osso
rows.address: Rua Bandeira Paulista, 520, São Paulo, 04532-001, Brazil
rows.description_en: An address that is much prized by meat-lovers in the Greater São Paulo area. Here, chef Renzo Garibaldi, who is known as the “Master Butcher” in his native Peru, has opened his first culinary venture in Brazil. His cuisine is based around meat sourced from sustainable producers, with the option of dry aged and different maturing times covering an array of different cuts. Beef is the star of the show here, available as ribeye, fillet mignon, picanha and short ribs, alongside special dry-aged pure Wagyu, Vaca Velha and Angus. Dishes such as ceviche, salad, Josper-grilled fish and the rice-based “arroz de costela” also feature on the menu in a modern, elegant space with an extensive and superb wine list.

rows.name: Yayá Comidaria Pop Brasileira
rows.address: Rua Gustavo Sampaio, 361 - Loja A, Rio de Janeiro, 22010-010, Brazil
rows.description_en: If you're looking for a restaurant close to the beach — in this case Leme beach, just north of Copacabana and a touch quieter and more family-friendly — this is a truly excellent choice, with a wonderfully casual atmosphere and under the direction of chef Andressa Cabral, well known for her starring role as a presenter on the television programme Iron Chef Brasil. Inside, the space surprises with its many pumpkin-shaped light fittings and a counter where you can also eat, and serves up heartfelt cooking rooted in Brazilian tradition, with well-updated dishes and fascinating African influences. The menu, with its very accessible prices, features some unmissable dishes — among them the delicious bolinho de banana com carne seca, a fried banana and salt-cod cake, and the so-called Peixe à Inajá, a heartfelt tribute to Dona Carmem Virginia, a towering figure in ancestral Brazilian cooking and in everything relating to female empowerment.

rows.name: Quinta da Henriqueta
rows.address: Rua Lopes Quintas, 165, Rio de Janeiro, 22460-010, Brazil
rows.description_en: This restaurant is a more refined take on its older sibling, Henriqueta, located in Leblon. In this charming restaurant near the Jardim Botânico, chef Antônio Minguins offers a menu brimming with traditional Portuguese dishes, with a particular focus on Azorean cooking. As one might expect, salt cod takes pride of place on the menu, appearing in a variety of interpretations: with coriander oil and a farofa — a toasted cassava crumb — of dehydrated olives, the traditional Gomes de Sá, with cream, à Transmontana... For meat lovers, there is no shortage of alternatives either, such as the Alcatra de carne — a traditional Azorean dish of beef slow-cooked for six hours in a clay pot — or the Chanfana de cabrito à moda do pato, a slow-braised kid goat prepared in the style of duck. The space, beyond its elegant interior featuring a beautiful glass-enclosed wine cellar, also has tables in the outdoor area, perfect for al fresco dining!

rows.name: Bicol Korean Cuisine
rows.address: Rua José Getúlio 422, São Paulo, 01509-000, Brazil
rows.description_en: Bicol is a must if you’re keen to try Korean barbecue-style cuisine. This classic address in the Liberdade district of the city has been run by a South Korean family for three generations. In this spacious restaurant, the tables have their own grills so that guests can cook meat (usually cut super-fine) to their individual taste. Dishes for sharing are the mainstay here, including the Burgogui, Garbi and Samguiopsar combos, as well as cuts of pure national Wagyu beef, always accompanied by Banchan (small side dishes of the day). The Bibimbap (a typical rice dish), soups, or classic dishes such as Topokki and Korean fried chicken are other interesting options on the menu, not forgetting the delicious kimchi, of course. Why not pair your food with the traditional soju, a typical Korean beverage with differing strengths of alcohol?

rows.name: Pobre Juan
rows.address: Rua Comendador Miguel Calfat 525, São Paulo, 04537-082, Brazil
rows.description_en: Inspired by traditional Argentine restaurants, Pobre Juan opened its first location in 2004 and today has a presence across all five regions of Brazil. Its concept is to offer high-quality produce in a rustic, relaxed setting, defined by warm wood tones, cosy lighting, and the irresistible aroma of the grill. Across all its locations, the selection process for the meats — as well as the fish and seafood featured on the menu — is carried out with the utmost rigour, from the careful sourcing of their origins to the ageing process. From the parrilla come premium cuts such as Bife Ancho, picanha, Ojo de Bife, and rack of lamb, alongside a selection of Wagyu beef. Over the grill, you'll also find options such as Amazonian pirarucu — a prized freshwater fish native to the Amazon — along with prawns... For pudding, we highly recommend trying the irresistible churros or the panqueques — delicate Argentine-style pancakes — both served with the traditional Argentine dulce de leche!

rows.name: Corrientes 348 - Marina da Glória
rows.address: Avenida Infante Dom Henrique, Rio de Janeiro, 20021-140, Brazil
rows.description_en: The name of this restaurant is a reference to the famous Argentinian tango “A Media Luz”, while the number 348 corresponds to the number of the street where the first of the brand’s ventures opened in Greater São Paulo. It overlooks the Marina da Glória, hence the spectacular views from tables on the terrace, and features several spacious dining rooms and an extensive glass-fronted wine cellar. The culinary focus is of course on Argentina and choice cuts of meats cooked on the grill, including specialities such as ribeye, centre cut ribeye, filet mignon with garlic, chorizo sausage and top sirloin, all accompanied by sides designed for sharing. To finish, the “dulce de leche” pancake served with sorbet is an authentic Argentinian dessert that is truly irresistible.

rows.name: Naga
rows.address: Rua Bandeira Paulista 385, São Paulo, 04532-011, Brazil
rows.description_en: A legendary Japanese restaurant in the city that has for a long time been a favourite address for aficionados of the country’s cuisine. It’s no surprise that the Nagayama group does not just have a single restaurant – in fact, in this area they own almost an entire block that includes the Bar do Naga, the Café do Naga etc. It is split between two floors, with access to the floor above via an attractive steep staircase. In the latter you’ll find two rooms: a waiting area with just a few tables, and a second more spacious room with a direct view of the pleasantly and subtly illuminated sushi bar. The extensive menu features a wide array of carpaccios, sushi, sashimi, uramaki, temaki, tartares and teppanyaki, and if there are several of you, you may want to try combination options such as the popular Naga Case 2 or the enticing Omakase-style tasting menu.

rows.name: Kosushi
rows.address: Rua Viradouro 139, São Paulo, 04538-110, Brazil
rows.description_en: The name of the restaurant has a direct link with Japanese philosophy as the word “ko” (which translates as “turtle”) is associated with long life and the symbolism of the number 1. Opened in 1988 by chef George Yuji Koshoji, it is now located at a different address (in the Itaim Bibi district), where it has become a popular meeting place for locals. It boasts a welcoming, contemporary ambience, soft lighting and a decor of bright colours, plus an impressive large balcony from where guests can watch their dishes being prepared. The extensive menu offers a variety of options such as gyosas, tartares, ussuzukuri, uramaki, sushi and sashimi, as well as hot dishes that include yakisoba, octopus yaki and Wagyu medallions. It also features a superb selection of sakis and innovative cocktails.

rows.name: Loup
rows.address: Dr. Mário Ferraz 528, São Paulo, 01453-011, Brazil
rows.description_en: Loup’s unique decor and atmosphere, featuring several dining spaces, designer details, lofty glass ceilings and an impressive vertical garden, have been very carefully curated, and provide the backdrop for an enticing fusion of cuisine from different parts of the world, prepared with top-quality ingredients. The menu includes delicious mini palm heart pastries with prawns, appetising dishes such as arroz de pato (rice with duck) that take you back to Portugal, and for dessert, the irresistible cannoli with a light yet crunchy dulce de leche and red berries, which transports you to the shores of Italy. It’s also worth taking time out to enjoy a cocktail in the lounge.

rows.name: Sud, O Pássaro Verde
rows.address: Rua Visconde de Carandaí 35, Rio de Janeiro, 22460-020, Brazil
rows.description_en: Walking into this restaurant is like entering the home of a friend, as you’ll need to knock on the door or announce your presence in order to be let in. Occupying a house in the quiet Jardim Botânico district, this is the domain of chef Roberta Sudbrack who describes it as a space in which to “tell and eat stories”. Inside, the decor is modest yet welcoming, with an impressive wood-fired oven next to the main dining room, plus a charming open kitchen, from which comforting home-style dishes emerge prepared with ingredients from small-scale local producers. As a result, the menu changes daily in line with market availability and freshness. However, one mainstay that is always on the menu is the superbly textured and irresistibly flavoured chocolate cake (“bolo de chocolate molhadinho”).

rows.name: Giuseppe Grill Leblon
rows.address: Avenida Bartolomeu Mitre 370, Rio de Janeiro, 22431-001, Brazil
rows.description_en: As the name clearly states, all the dishes (fish and meat) at this restaurant are cooked on the charcoal grill. The menu here includes dry-aged meat options (T-bone, prime rib, bone-in tenderloin etc). Other standout dishes include the Maminha (sirloin trip-tip), the Picanha supra sumo (supra sumo rump cap), the brand’s registered trademark, as well as the slow-cooked Uruguayan lamb shoulder served with its own jus. A number of fish and seafood options are also on display, which vary according to availability on the day. The decor here features exposed stone walls, wooden chairs and leather sofas, all of which combine to add a rustic-elegant touch. Not forgetting the extensive wine cellar in the basement, featuring over 400 labels from different countries.

rows.name: Chez Claude
rows.address: Rua Conde de Bernadotte 26 - Lojas Q e R, Rio de Janeiro, 22430-200, Brazil
rows.description_en: Run by the famous French chef Claude Troisgros, this dining space has plenty of detail to pique your interest. Firstly, the completely open kitchen in the centre of the room, enabling diners to watch dishes being prepared at close quarters that are based around French cuisine with the addition of some Brazilian-inspired elements and ingredients. And secondly, the fact that dishes on the classic menu are served in bowls for sharing, to add to the sense of family-style cooking. On the à la carte, which changes in line with the seasons of the year, we can recommend dishes such as the stuffed quail with herb farofa, chard confit and grape sauce. The impressively textured melted chocolate gâteau, served with crème fraîche, is the perfect way to round off your dining experience.

rows.name: Aprazível
rows.address: Rua Aprazível 62, Rio de Janeiro, 20241-270, Brazil
rows.description_en: Aprazível is a must for those who love a combination of delicious cuisine and nature. This family-run restaurant is located in hills surrounding the city in the Santa Teresa district, with its narrow winding streets and breathtaking views. Here, chef Ana Castilho conjures up a menu featuring organic and biodynamic ingredients from different regions around Brazil, yet without neglecting either creativity or a delicate touch. We can highly recommend the ceviche in a tucupi sauce with plantain chips, plus the delicious free-range “galinhada caipira” chicken, served with sausage from Minas Gerais, braised cabbage, a tasty pepper jelly and “surprise” beans. The restaurant also serves an array of superb drinks, including a vast selection of 100% natural wines as a perfect pairing for this culinary experience.

rows.name: Lilia
rows.address: Rua do Senado 45, Rio de Janeiro, 20231-005, Brazil
rows.description_en: A few metres from the conical Catedral de São Sebastião building, there is a singular restaurant with an unassuming façade that can easily go unnoticed among Lapa’s historic townhouses. Climbing a long, narrow staircase, you will discover a two‑storey establishment with brick walls that lend an industrial, pared‑back and spacious feel. Here, chef Yan Ramos runs a kitchen marked by his creativity, updated daily according to ingredient availability. At lunchtime, a fixed menu composed of three courses is served, while at dinner there is an eleven‑step tasting menu. Do not miss the unmissable Roasted beetroot served on curd, topped with tahini and herbs, and the crispy Barriga de porco pururuca (crispy‑skin pork belly) accompanied by smoked mashed potatoes, green apple and pork demi‑glace!

rows.name: Mr. Lam
rows.address: Rua Maria Angélica 21, Rio de Janeiro, 22470-201, Brazil
rows.description_en: Mr. Lam gained renowned for his culinary prowess in restaurants in New York and London, however he has run this modern, sophisticated eatery on the edge of the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon for almost two decades. In contrast with other gastronomic restaurants these days, the majority of dishes on the menu have been mainstays since it first opened, in so doing keeping with the tradition of offering the best Chinese cuisine. Featuring a hint of cutting-edge innovation as well as a focus on top-quality ingredients, the menu boasts memorable dishes such as the lightly battered and crispy Senhor Batista prawns, with a delicious sweet and sour sauce. The restaurant is laid out on three floors, with an attractive dining room and welcoming bar on the top floor that includes picture windows and a glass roof that provide lots of natural light and stunning views.

rows.name: Casa Santo Antônio
rows.address: Avenida João Carlos da Silva Borges 764, São Paulo, 04726-001, Brazil
rows.description_en: This extraordinary partnership is the result of a bond of friendship, the fruits of which are clearly visible in this superb gastronomic restaurant. Located somewhat off the beaten track in the southern section of São Paulo, it occupies a property built in the 1960s. It features a charming and elegant space with various dining rooms, a stunning bar and an outdoor terrace when the weather allows (a section of the glass-fronted kitchen is also visible to guests). The menu showcases an Italian influence with fresh homemade pastas, generous portions and moderate prices. An “executive” menu is also available during the week. Standout dishes here include the authentic and extremely delicious spaghetti alla carbonara, and the classic tiramisu, with its perfect creamy texture.

rows.name: Borgo Mooca
rows.address: Rua Barão De Tatuí, 302, São Paulo, 01226-030, Brazil
rows.description_en: This laid-back gastronomic retreat, nestled in the Santa Cecília neighbourhood, sets itself apart with its bold concept of "Punk Italian" — rooted in traditional Italian cooking, yet reinterpreted with creativity and a liberating sense of freedom. Founded by chef Bianca Giacomelli, the restaurant has made a name for itself through its seasonal cooking, combining classical techniques with a contemporary, experimental, and boldly disruptive approach. The atmosphere is further enriched by a counter overlooking the open kitchen, and a décor featuring original photographs by Neapolitan photographer Ciro Pipoli, capturing the everyday life of Naples. Not-to-be-missed dishes? The Tuna Akami Mille-feuille with parrilla-roasted beetroot and sour cream, the Gnocchi Fritti served with baby squid and Santa Catarina bottarga, and the house classic, Beef Wellington accompanied by mashed potato and demi-glace.

rows.name: Aiô
rows.address: Rua Áurea 307, São Paulo, 04015-070, Brazil
rows.description_en: Would you like to experience a distinctive culinary journey? Book a table at Aiô now. Here, the proposal is based on Taiwanese cuisine with international touches that take you on a journey through surprising flavours. Set on the same street as its sister restaurant, Mapu, the establishment features a characteristic glass façade and, inside, a bar at the entrance offering an intriguing variety of drinks: signature, re‑imagined and even Taiwanese‑inspired. The menu is straightforward and makes no distinction between starters and mains, which allows for sharing or opting for an individual tasting menu. A standout dish? O Crudo de Peixe (raw fish) made with aged fish, ponzu, chilli oil and finished with crunchy black‑rice popcorn.

rows.name: Mäska
rows.address: Rua Joana Angélica, 159, Rio de Janeiro, 22420-030, Brazil
rows.description_en: It's worth braving the frenetic traffic along Ipanema’s narrow streets to eat at this modern but relaxed restaurant with a contemporary bistro feel and a kitchen that opens onto the dining room to savour chef Danilo Parah’s innovative and contemporary cuisine. His recipes showcase ingredients of the very highest quality, including extremely fresh seafood, in dishes such as the unforgettable creamy rice with octopus, and the mouthwatering and perfectly cooked steak served with a truffled aligot mash. Not forgetting the masterfully prepared and delicate spaghetti with beurre blanc and braised prawns. The dining experience and atmosphere are enhanced by Mäska’s array of refreshing cocktails, which are an absolute must.

rows.name: Casa Rios
rows.address: Rua Deputado Lacerda Franco, 478, São Paulo, 05418-001, Brazil
rows.description_en: Restaurant Casa Rios embarks on a new chapter in Pinheiros, one of São Paulo's most lively and vibrant neighbourhoods. The charming venue, housed in a character-filled property whose verdant, plant-covered façade never fails to catch the eye, continues to have chef Rodrigo Aguiar at the helm of the kitchen. The kitchen continues to champion the values of traditional Brazilian gastronomy, with the essence of embers and smoked flavours serving as the guiding thread throughout; fittingly, the team here remains steadfast in their belief that fire, too, is an ingredient. The concept, which aims to be more dynamic and playful, now places an even greater focus on raw ingredients and the producers behind them. The à la carte menu — featuring dishes such as Beans, pork and kale, or Fusilli with Berkshire pork cheek shin, requeijão, a smooth Brazilian cream cheese, and Tahiti lime — is complemented by a set lunch menu on Friday afternoons.

rows.name: Terraço NOTIÊ
rows.address: Rua Formosa 157, São Paulo, 01049-000, Brazil
rows.description_en: Although only recently opened, this restaurant is already being talked about by the city’s foodie community. Located on the rooftop of the Shopping Light building, its design comes as a pleasant surprise as soon as you walk through the door thanks to its decor of yellow tones, glass-fronted kitchen enabling guests to watch the chefs hard at work and, first and foremost, the 18m panel on the ceiling depicting images of nature. At the helm in the kitchen is Paraíba-born chef Onildo Rocha who impresses with his use of typical Brazilian ingredients and combinations that result in intense and striking dishes. His recipes are based around his journeys to different Brazilian regions every season, and are showcased on 5-, 8- and 11-course tasting menus. The name of the restaurant is a fusion between one of the country’s most colourful birds, the tanager (tiê in Portuguese) and the Portuguese word for night (noite).

rows.name: Cala del Tanit
rows.address: Rua Pais De Araújo, 147, São Paulo, 04531-090, Brazil
rows.description_en: A new culinary venture courtesy of chef Oscar Bosch, who has been on the rise in São Paulo's food scene since he opened the successful Tanit in the Jardins district of the city. Located in Itaim Bibi, in one of the typical three-storey houses in this neighbourhood, Cala del Tanit boasts a terrace at the entrance and a contemporary interior with a predominance of wood, an open-view kitchen and a counter where cocktails are also prepared for guests. The menu retains the essence of Mediterranean cuisine, with Spanish dishes such as tomato gazpacho and delicious rice dishes (Paella Marinera and duck rice socarrat, with grilled octopus and aioli), although the culinary repertoire here also includes an array of pasta dishes and a few Asian touches. A space for small private events, called Sala X, is also available.

rows.name: Le Jardin
rows.address: Rua Itapeva, 435, São Paulo, 01332-000, Brazil
rows.description_en: A true oasis of sophistication and serenity, enveloped by nature amid the bustle of the city. Le Jardin offers a luxurious setting inspired by a winter garden, where both the décor and the atmosphere are impossible to overlook. The concept here is rooted in classic international cuisine, with carefully crafted dishes, in a space that is ideal for dining at any hour of the day. In the morning, breakfast is served with house specialities and healthy options to choose from. As the day unfolds, a varied all-day menu is available, while evenings bring an alternative selection alongside a Kosher menu, available on prior reservation. Our suggestion? Try the lamb ossobuco — a slow-braised lamb shank — served with linguine in a truffle fonduta with watercress and a herb farofa, a toasted cassava crumb, and the suckling pig shoulder with organic carrots and a sweet-and-sour pork roti sauce — dishes that are sure to exceed your expectations!

rows.name: Marena Cucina
rows.address: Rua Pais De Araújo 138, São Paulo, 04531-090, Brazil
rows.description_en: In the heart of Itaim Bibi, one of São Paulo's most sophisticated districts, you’ll come across this Italian restaurant that oozes personality, both in its warm Mediterranean-inspired decor combining exposed stone and wood, and its unique cuisine. Although it offers an array of pasta and specialities from across the country (Rome, Naples, Tuscany etc), the aim here is to also incorporate the specific flavours of the Puglia region in the “heel of the boot” in the deep south of the country. The cuisine is unpretentious yet delicious, and is showcased in dishes such as artisanally produced Ficchi & Aceto IGP burrata, grilled octopus, and Tagliolini Marena with fresh pasta, prawns, octopus, squid and pomodorini. The mouthwatering prosciuttos here are also a must.

rows.name: Rufino Parrilla
rows.address: Rua Tubira, 43, Rio de Janeiro, 22441-070, Brazil
rows.description_en: If you’re keen to experience cooking on an authentic Argentinian parrilla grill without the inconvenience of leaving Leblon, a visit to Rufino is a must. This restaurant, already famous in Buenos Aires, has now opened an outlet in Rio de Janeiro. The menu is prepared by Argentinian chef Agustin Brañas, who brings with him the experience of working in prestigious restaurants outside of the country. In this elegant space, reminiscent of the typical parrilla eateries in neighbouring Argentina, the highlights are undoubtedly the exceptional cuts of meats (such as sirloin, Angus skirt steak, Argentinian Tomahawk, ribeye etc) cooked on the open grill. Desserts include the classic pancake with dulce de leche and banana ice cream. The extensive selection of Argentinian wines is the perfect complement to your meal here.

rows.name: Makoto San
rows.address: Rua Leandro Dupré 108, São Paulo, 04025-010, Brazil
rows.description_en: Fancy a little trip to Japan? Ring the doorbell at the entrance of this spot, and you can make that dream come true — no jet lag required. The moment you step into this extremely simple, rustic-minimalist, and unpretentious space, you are in the hands of chef Helio Makoto Yamashita, a sushi master who has refined his omakase menu over the years, drawing on outstanding technique and the exceptional quality of the fish he works with. There are a handful of tables, generally small, but the best seat in the house is at the counter, where you can watch up close the preparation of both the sushi and the sashimi. Details that make all the difference? As you enjoy your meal, the chef celebrates the singular culture of Meibutsu Ryouri — the love and respect for Japan's regional specialities — enthusiastically sharing fascinating stories about the ingredients he uses and anecdotes from his nearly 10 years living in Japan... Live the experience!

rows.name: Shin Zushi
rows.address: Rua Afonso de Freitas 169, São Paulo, 04006-050, Brazil
rows.description_en: If you're on the lookout for a Japanese restaurant where you can eat well in the Paraíso district, this is a perfect option, underlined by the fact that most of its clientele have Asian roots. Shin Zushi has a strong family personality as the business was originally created by the father and is currently run by two brothers (Ken and Nobu Mizumoto). The focus here is on classic Japanese cuisine which can be enjoyed at the counter with an Omakase menu, or at its more traditional tables with exclusive à la carte service. We particularly enjoyed the Omakase menu and service at the counter, which was very friendly and relaxed, and featured superb combinations such as the oyster with horse mackerel.

rows.name: Piselli
rows.address: Rua Padre João Manuel 1253, São Paulo, 01411-001, Brazil
rows.description_en: Piselli is the Italian word for “pea” and this vegetable is highly significant for the owner Juscelino Pereira who still maintains his custom of decorating every plate with three peas. Nowadays, the brand has three restaurants in São Paulo and one in Brasilia, and the cuisine is the same in each of them: namely, high-quality Italian cooking inspired by the Piedmont region. Dishes here are well prepared and full of flavour. Among them, we recommend the incredible “burrata calda al tartufo”, baked in delicious focaccia. Follow this, perhaps, with the homemade tortelloni filled with mozzarella di bufala and served with a fresh tomato and basil sauce, and the classic ossobuco alla milanese with saffron rice. In summary, a simply wonderful culinary experience.

rows.name: Nosso
rows.address: Rua Maria Quitéria 91, Rio de Janeiro, 22410-040, Brazil
rows.description_en: An exclusive restaurant with three completely different floors: on the first, a bar; on the second, a dining space with an intimate ambience for a pleasant supper; and on the third, an outdoor terrace. Here, the relaxed cuisine, which is described by chef Bruno Katz as “contemporary”, features dishes that combine different food cultures from around the world in a creative and harmonious way. One example is the glazed octopus served with fried rice, kewpie mayonnaise, moyashi and nira, which is simply divine and cooked to perfection. Bartender Daniel Estevan elevates his concoctions to another level, combining classic drinks with his experience of the Amazon to create cocktails such as the surprising Tacacá Sour, with its mix of jambu, tucupi, cupuaçu and lemon. An extraordinary experience!

rows.name: Ama.zo - Cozinha Peruana
rows.address: Rua Guaianases 1149, São Paulo, 01204-001, Brazil
rows.description_en: This restaurant occupies the charming garden of an old property known as the Casa da Don'Anna, a 20C house with a strong coffee legacy. The ambience here is delightful, protected by the vagaries of the weather by an almost invisible roof, and features large jabuticabeira trees, tables laid out in the garden, and a semi-open kitchen to the rear. Here, Peruvian chef Enrique Paredes conjures up Andean cuisine that is reinterpreted through the use of local ingredients, strong flavours, pleasant textures and subtle nuances from the Amazon region. Among the starters, the fresh oysters with a Japanese ponzu sauce, physalis and black massago stands out, followed, perhaps, by a main of ossobuco cooked at low temperature with an Arequipeño sauce, and accompanied by a cassava millefeuille. Lovers of cacao will adore the intense and absolutely delicious chocolate x 4!

rows.name: Vista
rows.address: Avenida Pedro Álvares Cabral 1301 - 8º andar, São Paulo, 04094-050, Brazil
rows.description_en: Perched on the top floor of the MAC-USP (Museu de Arte Contemporânea da Universidade de São Paulo), this restaurant commands spectacular views of Parque Ibirapuera and the entire city in a full 360 degrees. The concept celebrates traditional Brazilian cooking, with signature dishes inspired by the country's diverse regions and crafted from high-quality ingredients. On Saturdays, the chef's classic feijoada — the rich, slow-cooked black bean and pork stew that is a cornerstone of Brazilian culinary tradition — takes centre stage; on Sundays, the Vista Mar menu makes its appearance, drawing inspiration from caiçara coastal cuisine and featuring irresistible options such as Camarão na moranga, a prawn and butternut squash dish that comfortably serves two; during the week, à la carte dishes and a set lunch menu are on offer. The experience is rounded off by an extensive selection of classic and house cocktails, a wide-ranging wine list, and the Balcão Vista — a perfect spot that is simply perfect for anyone wishing to soak in the view over a pre-dinner drink or aperitif.

rows.name: Amadeus
rows.address: Rua Haddock Lobo 807, São Paulo, 01420-002, Brazil
rows.description_en: No description of Amadeus can be made without mentioning the Masano family, along with their passion, enthusiasm and dreams. Thanks to rave reviews of their cooking from friends, they decided to open a restaurant known as “fish corner” in São Paulo. Today, the kitchen is overseen by chef Bella Masano, the owners’ daughter, who embellishes the menu with her innovative culinary creations alongside classic dishes which have been given a contemporary makeover. Her cooking is showcased on an à la carte and tasting menu which includes options such as fresh oysters from the family’s own beds in Florianópolis. Amadeus’ signature dishes include the shrimp “à paulista”, prepared with olive oil and garlic, which is full of flavour and perfect for sharing, and the “moqueca Amadeus”, a stew with fish and shrimp, served with plantain and onion farofa – an exquisite combination!

rows.name: Cantaloup
rows.address: Rua Manuel Guedes 474, São Paulo, 04536-070, Brazil
rows.description_en: A true oasis of sophistication that impresses at first sight. Housed in a former bread factory, the space preserves its lofty ceiling height and reveals a spacious, refined dining room, featuring a classic-style bar. Alongside it, a charming waiting area, sheltered by a retractable roof, allows abundant natural light to pour in, creating a pleasant, harmonious atmosphere between the greenery and the fountain that lends freshness to the setting. Chef Valdir Oliveira presents an appealing menu, built on internationally inspired dishes with a strong Italian influence, standing out for its variety of risottos and pastas. Among the starters, we particularly enjoyed the Ceviche de vieiras (scallop ceviche), served with caju (cashew), quinoa crocante (crispy quinoa) and vinagrete de pimenta de cheiro (aromatic chilli vinaigrette), and, as a main course, the Medalhão de filet mignon (fillet mignon medallion) with penne gratinado (gratinated penne) and molho rôti (roast jus). The à la carte offering is complemented by an enticing set lunch menu available throughout the week!

rows.name: Rubaiyat Rio
rows.address: Rua Jardim Botânico 971, Rio de Janeiro, 22470-051, Brazil
rows.description_en: Located in the Jockey Club Brasileiro within the boundaries of the city’s botanical gardens, this restaurant boasts breathtaking views where you can enjoy a meal on the terrace to a picture-postcard backdrop that features the horse-racing track as well as the statue of Christ the Redeemer. Inside, there is a large dining room with a counter that is home to the kitchen, where a large glass window provides views of the churrasco grill. Renowned for its array of premium meats and for managing its own production, the restaurant offers more than ten different cuts, although fish, seafood, rice and a variety of sides also feature on the menu. On Saturdays, don't miss the chance to try the traditional feijoada stew, made with prime cuts of meat, along with milkshakes and an incredible dessert buffet!

rows.name: Aya Japanese Cuisine
rows.address: Avenida Pedroso de Morais 141, São Paulo, 05419-000, Brazil
rows.description_en: This attractive property with a contemporary ambience and minimalist decor has a good location in a busy part of the city, just a few metres from the famous Avenida Rebouças. It is under the baton of sushi chef Juraci Pereira (better known as “Jura”) who, after working as Jun Sakamoto’s right-hand man for 11 years, decided to open his own venture in collaboration with his business partner Beto Ganme. Downstairs, where guests can sit at the counter to watch the expert hands of the chefs in action, the atmosphere is more intimate, while the upstairs is more modern and cosy. The cuisine includes a special Aya omakase menu, various types of sashimi, sushi (à la carte and combos), makimonos and hot dish options.

rows.name: Fogo de Chão
rows.address: Rua Augusta 2077, São Paulo, 01413-000, Brazil
rows.description_en: The Fogo de Chão restaurant is much more than just a place to eat as it represents Brazil’s churrasco tradition that has won admirers in different parts of the world. The origins of this method for cooking meat date back to the gauchos who discovered that skewering pieces of meat on wooden sticks and placing them around a fire transformed a simple cut of meat into a true delicacy. Served as part of “rodizio” all-you-can-eat format, the extensive selection includes beef, lamb and pork, as well as the famous prime rib and dry-aged meats (only available on the à la carte). To accompany the superb choice of meat, there’s also an extensive buffet of salads, rice dishes, carpaccios, cheeses and sausages. In total, there are five Fogo de Chão restaurants in São Paulo, all of which boast a comprehensive wine list. The new addition at the Jardins restaurant is a space dedicated to cigar-lovers.

rows.name: A Figueira Rubaiyat
rows.address: Rua Haddock Lobo 1738, São Paulo, 01414-002, Brazil
rows.description_en: The backdrop here is definitely a surprise, thanks to the majestic Bengal fig, a century-old tree that attracts admiring glances inside this restaurant. The glass roof adds a special touch, enabling guests to admire the immensity of its crown and branches to the full. In keeping with its sister property in the famous Faria Lima, the cuisine is based around the "farm to table” concept. Both the beef and pork are produced at the group’s own farms and distributed throughout its franchises. Dishes include baby beef, Denver steak, filet mignon, master beef and “tirita de picanha”, all of which are cooked to perfection, although the menu also features a variety of fish, rice and pasta options. Enhance your dining experience with the superb array of labels available on the wine list.

rows.name: Dinho's
rows.address: Alameda Santos 86, São Paulo, 01418-000, Brazil
rows.description_en: Dinho's was opened by Fuad Zegaib (the creator of the strip steak) six decades ago. Nowadays, the restaurant is run by chef Paulo Zegaib, the founder’s son. Occupying a new home on the ground floor of the Hotel Qoya, in the Paraíso section of the city (there’s also a Dinho’s in the Jardins district), it features a spacious, classically furnished main dining room, which is entirely glass-fronted and enclosed by a beautiful vertical garden plus a colourful open kitchen to one side. Renowned for its longevity in this bustling capital city, the restaurant offers superb cuts of beef, as well as feijoada on Thursdays and Saturdays, a buffet of salads and desserts, plus a copious seafood buffet on Fridays.

rows.name: Fasano Trattoria
rows.address: Rua Iguatemi s/n, São Paulo, 01451-010, Brazil
rows.description_en: Set against a remarkable backdrop, surrounded by some of São Paulo's most imposing landmarks — including the sleek, modern Pátio Malzoni and, to its left, the Casa Bandeirista, a significant example of 17th-century Brazilian colonial architecture — this elegant trattoria emerges as a striking contrast, paying homage to southern Italy through a décor that blends wood, leather, and the colours of traditional Italian football clubs. The menu celebrates classic recipes and dishes inspired by the region of Naples and the island of Capri, including the memorable linguine alle vongole con pomodorini — linguine with clams and cherry tomatoes — the timeless spaghetti alla carbonara, and, among the main courses, the succulent polpettone al forno, a slow-baked Italian-style meatloaf. The space also boasts a delightful outdoor terrace, perfect for those wishing to enjoy their meal in a tranquil setting surrounded by a beautiful garden.

rows.name: Chef Rouge
rows.address: Rua Bela Cintra 2238, São Paulo, 01415-002, Brazil
rows.description_en: An authentic French bistro, both in terms of its black façade and red awning and its elegant, welcoming interior. The main dining space is complemented by a charming terrace at the entrance, adorned with two impressive trees and with candlelight in the evening. Some of the tables are also occupied by adorable, large red teddy bears that add to the delightful atmosphere. Understandably, the culinary focus and star of the show is classic French cooking with a contemporary touch that is showcased by top-quality ingredients and delicately prepared dishes. These include the grilled foie gras with figs, served with bitter chocolate, and the classic roast duck breast with orange sauce accompanied by gaufrettes potatoes. The incredible Eclair XXL provides the perfect finale!

rows.name: Paparoto Cucina
rows.address: Av. Pres. Juscelino Kubitschek, 2041 - Térreo, São Paulo, 04543-011, Brazil
rows.description_en: Part of the luxury JK Iguatemi complex, this restaurant has a spacious and modern setting with a decor that includes plants and subdued lighting that accentuates the illuminated Italian phrase “Se non ora quando?” (“If not now, when”). Famous chef Dayse Paparoto, who won the first edition of Brazil’s Professional Masterchef, showcases his Italian-inspired menu with an authentic and innovative touch that is based around fresh, top-quality ingredients. The menu features an array of options, such as the excellent egg yolk ravioli with ricotta and spinach, served with a soft egg yolk. Other options include fresh pastas and risottos, although the desserts steal the show here, highlighting the extreme creativity of the chef in dishes such as tiramisu, served with a candy floss tree, which comes as a complete surprise.

rows.name: Metzi
rows.address: Rua João Moura, 861, São Paulo, 05412-002, Brazil
rows.description_en: Ever wondered what a fusion of Brazilian and Mexican cooking would taste like? The answer is... simply wonderful! Chefs Luana Sabino and Eduardo Nava Ortiz, who met while working at a restaurant in New York, decided to pool their know-how to treat our palates to an incredible concept. The menu marries the techniques and traditions of authentic Mexican cooking with fresh Brazilian ingredients, creating dishes that champion seasonality and celebrate the best of each ingredient. You can choose à la carte or go for the nine-moment tasting menu, which includes the refreshing starter Aguachile de maracujá, sashimi e sauva, passion-fruit aguachile with sashimi and saúva ants; the punchy Camarão al ajillo, queijo tulha e ovas de salmão, prawns al ajillo with tulha cheese and salmon roe; and lightly spicy Wagyu beef with okra and Brazilian shishito peppers. To accompany the experience, there’s a tempting line-up of cocktails!

rows.name: Maza
rows.address: Rua Manuel Guedes, 243, São Paulo, 04536-070, Brazil
rows.description_en: As well as a highly enjoyable dining experience, Maza boasts a relaxing and welcoming setting, where the combination of wood and soft tones is clearly evident as soon as you walk through the door – a decor embellished by the beautiful cherry tree. The cuisine here is based around classic Japanese fare with a modern and personalised touch, including some Korean dishes. The different types of menus on offer include a seven-course option called Shinrai (served exclusively at table), the Omakase (only available at the bar counter), an à la carte. Exquisite dishes include karasumi, ussuzukuri, Wagyu tataki, “shake butter”, as well as sushi, sashimi, temaki. An impressive choice of sakes and cocktails completes the picture.

rows.name: Henriqueta
rows.address: Rua Aristides Espínola, 121, Rio de Janeiro, 22440-050, Brazil
rows.description_en: This “tasca” style restaurant in the southern part of Rio de Janeiro showcases the best of Portuguese cuisine in a bright environment with a glass façade, open kitchen and Portuguese ceramic decoration. The cuisine on offer dispenses with unnecessary frills, focusing on the quality of the ingredients and dishes designed for sharing, among which the “biff-anas açorianas”, a crispy bread sandwich filled with pork escalope marinated in wine and garlic, stands out. As a main course, we recommend the tender octopus “a lagareiro” roasted in oil, served with onion confit and mashed potatoes, followed by the “toucinho do céu” made with egg yolks, almonds and cinnamon, an authentic Portuguese dish if ever there was one!

rows.name: Clan BBQ
rows.address: Rua Dias Ferreira, 233 Loja B, Rio de Janeiro, 22431 050, Brazil
rows.description_en: To the backdrop of a neon sign “Não apague o meu fogo” (“Don’t put out my fire”) clearly visible above the door, chefs Pepo Figueiredo and Newton Rique showcase cuisine in which fire plays a key role here, enabling them to prepare fresh ingredients imbued with a special flavour. In this industrial-style ambience with a predominance of raw concrete, a sturdy tree takes centre stage in the middle of the dining room. There’s also the option of sitting at the counter by the grill to watch dishes and cocktails being prepared at close quarters. The menu is of course heavily focused on barbecued meats, although you’ll also find other options such as vegetables, fish and burgers. Dishes you won’t want to miss include the creamy oxtail croquettes and cubes of smoked tongue with aioli. The succulent French rack of lamb, served with chimichurri, is cooked to perfection.

rows.name: Spicy Fish
rows.address: Rua Maria Quitéria, 99, Rio de Janeiro, 22410-040, Brazil
rows.description_en: A restaurant that is the talk of the town when it comes to Asian cuisine, a reputation enhanced by the magnificent building in which it is situated – a four-storey property featuring a decor of neutral tones, soft lighting and lots of plants which add a touch of freshness to the space. The cuisine created by chef Emerson Kim is a fusion of Japanese and Korean cooking, showcased via well-presented dishes with a unique flavour. The menu is extensive and for those unsure what to order, the chef’s selection includes two portions of nigiri, sashimi and the “house special”. Hot dishes include the reinterpretation of the Bibimbap, the finishing touches to which are always added at the table, and the delicious Kagoshima wagyu beef, known as Hot Stone.

rows.name: Rudä
rows.address: Rua Garcia D'Ávila, 118, Rio de Janeiro, 22421-010, Brazil
rows.description_en: At Rudä, chef Danilo Parah champions what he calls “emotional and creative cuisine” in a contemporary bistro-style setting featuring different ambiences and a private room on the first floor. His dishes are colourful, generous and highly flavourful with little fear when it comes to combining lots of ingredients. It’s hard to beat the octopus with jambu fruit (a dish with a profusion of colours and textures that includes pasta cooked in a moqueca sauce) or the delicious cheesecake with an almond tuile, guava syrup and strawberry compote, all of which will linger long in the memory. The hospitality is on a par with the food, the latter presented on a varied à la carte that showcases local ingredients in addition to an “executive” menu.

rows.name: Les Présidents
rows.address: Rua Da Consolação 3527, São Paulo, 01416-001, Brazil
rows.description_en: Under the helm of famous chef Érick Jacquin, best known for his appearances on MasterChef, this bistro-style restaurant serves sophisticated cuisine inspired by the chef’s French roots. Occupying a striking building with a completely black façade and red doors, the interior is no less impressive with its myriad paintings and embellishments that add to the typically French ambience. To enjoy the experience to the full, we recommend the delicious langoustine ravioli served with vegetables and a Sauternes emulsion with ginger, or the classic duck foie gras, accompanied by caramelised bananas, an orange reduction and bitter chocolate. A seven-course surprise tasting menu created by the chef is also available, alongside the à la carte and a midweek “executive”-style menu.
